title: Rama, Sita and the Golden Deer
bigQuestion: Why do people keep a promise when it is hard?

story.title: The Shining Deer
story.kicker: A golden deer leaps through the forest, and Sita asks Rama to catch it.
paragraphs: The forest is green and quiet. Rama and Sita live in a small hut. Rama's brother Lakshmana lives there too. They have lived in the forest for many years.
One morning, something shines between the trees. It is a deer! Its coat is gold. Its spots look like silver. Sita smiles. "Please catch that deer for me," she says.
Rama picks up his bow. He runs after the deer. The deer runs far, far away into the trees. But this deer is not a real deer. It is a trick.
What will happen to Sita now? This very old story tells us. Families in India and in Illinois still love to tell it today.
story.think: Sita saw something beautiful and wanted it. Have you ever wanted something you saw?

lessons.title: The Ramayana
lessons.mainIdea: The Ramayana is a very old story from India.
reading: The *Ramayana* is a story from India. It is very, very old. People have told it for more than 2,000 years.
A poet named Valmiki told the story in a long poem. Today people tell it in books, songs, plays and cartoons.

words.d: a very old story from India about Prince Rama and Princess Sita

look.title: A Grandma Tells a Story
look.text: Look at the grandma on the soft couch. A small boy sits on her lap. She holds an old book with bright pictures. She points to a prince with a bow. She says, "This is Rama."
look.prompt: Who tells you stories at home? What is your favorite one?

check.q: Where does the Ramayana come from?
check.why: The Ramayana is a very old story from India.

check.q: Is the Ramayana a new story or an old story?
choices: A story from a TV show made this year
check.why: People have told the Ramayana for more than 2,000 years.

check.q: Who told the Ramayana as a long poem?
check.why: Hindus remember the poet Valmiki as the teller of the Ramayana poem.

lessons.title: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana
lessons.mainIdea: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana are the main people in the story.
reading: Rama is a prince. He is kind and brave. Sita is a princess. She is Rama's wife. She is kind and strong.
Lakshmana is Rama's brother. He stays with Rama always. Many Hindus honor Rama as a form of God. They love Sita too.

words.d: the son of a king and queen
the daughter of a king and queen, or a prince's wife

look.title: Three Friends in a Picture
look.text: Look at the picture. A prince holds a bow. His skin is painted blue. Many artists paint Rama blue. A princess in yellow stands by him. His brother stands close by.
look.prompt: Point to Rama. Point to Sita. How can you tell who is who?

check.why: In the Ramayana, Rama is a prince.
Lakshmana is Rama's brother. He stays with Rama.

check.q: How do many Hindus honor Rama?
check.why: Many Hindus honor Rama as a form of God.

lessons.title: The King's Promise
lessons.mainIdea: Rama goes to the forest to keep his father's promise.
reading: Rama's father is King Dasharatha. Long ago, the king made a promise to Queen Kaikeyi. He said he would give her two wishes.
Now the queen asks for her wishes. She wants her son Bharata to be king. She wants Rama to live in the forest for fourteen years.
The king is very sad. But a promise is a promise. Rama is calm. He says, "I will go, Father."

words.d: saying you will surely do something

look.title: Rama Says Yes
look.text: Rama tells the queen he will go to the forest. He says he will do what his father promised. He is not angry.
look.cite: Retold from Valmiki's Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda (Book 2)
look.prompt: Rama is not angry. Why do you think he says yes?

check.why: King Dasharatha, Rama's father, made a promise to Queen Kaikeyi.

check.q: How long will Rama live in the forest?
check.why: Queen Kaikeyi asks that Rama live in the forest for fourteen years.

choices: He keeps the promise and goes
check.why: Rama keeps his father's promise, even though it is hard.

lessons.title: Into the Forest
lessons.mainIdea: Sita and Lakshmana choose to go with Rama.
reading: Rama must go to the forest. Sita says, "I will go with you." Lakshmana says, "I will go too."
They leave the palace. They wear simple clothes. They walk into the big forest. They build a little hut to live in.

words.d: a big place with many trees and animals

look.title: Who Went to the Forest?
look.prompt: Count them. How many people went to the forest?

check.q: Who goes to the forest with Rama?
check.why: Sita and Lakshmana choose to go with Rama.

check.q: Where do they live in the forest?
check.why: They build a little hut in the forest.

choices: She wants to stay with Rama
check.why: Sita wants to be with Rama, so she goes too.

lessons.title: A Deer That Is a Trick
lessons.mainIdea: The golden deer is a trick to take Rama away.
reading: Sita sees a golden deer. She asks Rama to catch it. Rama runs after the deer. Then Lakshmana goes to find Rama.
The deer was a trick. Now Sita is alone. Nobody is there to keep her safe. That was the plan.

words.d: something that fools you on purpose

look.title: Too Good to Be True
look.text: Look at the deer in the picture. Its fur shines like gold. Its spots shine like silver. No real deer looks like this.
look.prompt: What clue tells you this deer is not a real deer?

check.q: What does Sita ask Rama to do?
check.why: Sita sees the golden deer and asks Rama to catch it.

check.q: What is the golden deer really?
check.why: In the Ramayana, the golden deer is a trick.

check.q: Who is left alone at the hut?
check.why: Rama and Lakshmana go away, so Sita is left alone.

lessons.title: Ravana Takes Sita
lessons.mainIdea: Ravana, king of Lanka, carries Sita far away.
reading: Ravana is the king of Lanka. The story says he has ten heads. He comes to the hut. He carries Sita away in his flying chariot.
A brave bird named Jatayu tries to stop him. Sita drops her jewelry as a clue. Rama will need help to find her.

words.d: the ten-headed king of Lanka in the Ramayana

look.title: A Trail of Jewels
look.text: As Ravana flies, Sita drops her jewels to the ground below. She hopes Rama will find them.
look.cite: Retold from Valmiki's Ramayana, Aranya Kanda (Book 3) and Kishkindha Kanda (Book 4)
look.prompt: Why is dropping the jewels a smart idea?

check.why: Ravana, the king of Lanka, carries Sita away.

check.q: How many heads does the story give Ravana?
check.why: The Ramayana says Ravana has ten heads.

check.q: What does Sita drop as a clue?
check.why: Sita drops her jewelry so Rama can find her trail.

choices: A very old story from India
review.why: The Ramayana is a very old story from India.

review.q: Why does Rama go to the forest?
review.why: Rama keeps King Dasharatha's promise to Queen Kaikeyi.

review.q: What does Sita see in the forest?
review.why: Sita sees a shining golden deer.
Ravana is the king of Lanka.

review.q: How do many Hindus honor Rama?
review.why: Many Hindus honor Rama as a form of God.
